  Click to open a pre-filled email template, fill in the fields, and send it to `support@langdock.com`
</Card>

<Accordion title="What to include in your submission">
  The email template contains these fields:

  * **Company and product website**: your company name and the product's website
  * **Support or technical contact**: who we can reach with technical questions, if different from you
  * **MCP server name**: the name as it should appear in the directory
  * **MCP server URL**: the remote URL users connect to
  * **Documentation URL**: public documentation for your MCP server
  * **Transport**: Remote/HTTP, Remote/SSE, or other
  * **Authentication**: OAuth, API key, bearer token, none, or other, plus brief connection instructions. Do not send secrets.
  * **What can users do with this MCP server?**: a one-sentence description for the directory listing, plus main capabilities, example tasks, and any account or plan requirements
  * **Testing**: a test instance and account without 2FA, or a sign-up link where we can create a demo account
  * **Logo**: attach a square PNG or SVG logo
  * **Confirmation**: confirm this is an official remotely hosted MCP server and that Langdock may test it for directory review
</Accordion>

<Warning>
  We only list MCP servers we have tested ourselves. Without working test access, we can't add your server to the directory.
</Warning>

## How to Connect an MCP Server

You need the **Create integrations** permission to add a remote MCP server. If **Add integration** is not visible, ask a workspace admin to grant you this permission or create the integration for you.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Navigate to Integrations">
    Open **Integrations** from the main navigation.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Add Integration">
    Click **Add integration**, choose **Start from scratch**, then select **Connect remote MCP**.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Enter Server Details">
    Copy the **Server URL** from the directory above. Enter it and choose an **Authentication method**.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Create and Connect">
    Click **Create and connect**. For **OAuth 2.0 Manual (Authorization Code + PKCE)**, click **Create**, configure the client, save it, then add a connection.
  </Step>

  <Step title="List Server Features">
    For **API Key**, **OAuth 2.0 (Dynamic Client Registration)**, and **OAuth 2.0 Manual (Authorization Code + PKCE)**, click **List Server Features** after creating a connection. Select the tools and resources you want, then click **Save**. For None, Langdock saves all discovered capabilities automatically.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Start Using">
    Your MCP server is now available in agents, chats, and workflows.
  </Step>
</Steps>

For detailed setup instructions, see the [MCP Integration Guide](/en/using-langdock/guides/integrations/mcp/mcp).

***

## Authentication Types Explained

| Auth Type                                        | Description                                                       | What You Need                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **None**                                         | No authentication required                                        | Server URL. Langdock tests the server and discovers its capabilities automatically.                                                              |
| **OAuth 2.0 (Dynamic Client Registration)**      | OAuth 2.0 with automatic client registration and token management | Server URL, then create and connect to authenticate. If Dynamic Client Registration fails, use **OAuth 2.0 Manual (Authorization Code + PKCE)**. |
| **OAuth 2.0 Manual (Authorization Code + PKCE)** | OAuth 2.0 with manually configured client details                 | OAuth Client ID, Client Secret, Authorization URL, Token URL, and required scopes                                                                |
| **API Key**                                      | Key based authentication with a selectable header format          | API key and the header format expected by the server. For bearer authentication, select **Authorization: Bearer** under **API Key Header Type**. |

A listing labeled **OAuth DCR** or **OAuth 2.0 (Dynamic Client Registration)** maps directly to that product choice. For a listing labeled only **OAuth**, try **OAuth 2.0 (Dynamic Client Registration)** first. Use **OAuth 2.0 Manual (Authorization Code + PKCE)** when the server does not support Dynamic Client Registration.

Any label that mentions **Bearer Token** maps to **API Key** authentication with **Authorization: Bearer** as the **API Key Header Type**. A label with a slash means the server accepts either listed method. **None / Optional** maps to **None** unless you need optional authenticated features. For **Custom**, follow the server documentation.

If a listing shows **SSE** as its authentication type, treat **SSE** as a transport and check the provider's documentation for the actual authentication method.

# Building MCP Servers with MCP Apps
Source: https://docs.langdock.com/en/using-langdock/integrations/mcp-ui

MCP Apps is an official MCP extension that lets your server return interactive UIs rendered directly inside Langdock and other MCP hosts.

## What is MCP Apps?

MCP Apps is an official extension to the Model Context Protocol that lets MCP servers return interactive HTML/JavaScript interfaces — rendered directly in the host application (Langdock, Claude Desktop, VS Code, etc.) — instead of plain text.

<Info>
  **MCP vs MCP Apps**

  Standard MCP tools return text or structured data. MCP Apps tools can additionally return a fully interactive UI — forms, dashboards, visualizations — rendered inside the conversation.
</Info>

## How It Works

<Steps>
  <Step title="Tool declares a UI resource">
    Your tool definition includes a `_meta.ui.resourceUri` pointing to a `ui://` resource served by your MCP server. This tells compatible hosts that the tool has a UI component.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Host fetches and renders the UI">
    When the LLM calls the tool, the host fetches the HTML from your server and renders it in a **sandboxed iframe**. In Langdock, the iframe appears as a standalone output in the chat after the tool call. On desktop, you can open it in the side panel or show it in the chat.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Bidirectional communication">
    The UI and host communicate via **JSON-RPC over `postMessage`**. Your app can request tool calls, update the model's context, and receive results — all without leaving the conversation.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## View MCP Apps in Chat

When an MCP tool declares a UI resource, Langdock displays the MCP App as a standalone output in the chat after the tool finishes. The app appears outside the tool call details. Standard MCP tools without a UI resource continue to show their regular output.

On desktop, select **Open in side panel** to move the app to a resizable side panel while you continue the conversation. Select **Show in chat** to return it to the chat.

## Security Model

MCP Apps runs in a sandboxed environment. The host controls what your app can access:

| Layer                  | What it does                                                                                                      |
| ---------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Iframe sandbox**     | Isolates the app from the parent page and other tabs                                                              |
| **App HTML**           | Langdock renders the HTML returned by your MCP server directly in the sandbox without inspecting or sanitizing it |
| **Enabled resources**  | Apps can read only resources enabled for the integration                                                          |
| **Auditable JSON-RPC** | All app-to-host communication is loggable                                                                         |
| **Confirmation gate**  | Apps cannot call tools or read resources that require confirmation                                                |

## Building Your Own

The official SDK is `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps`. It works with React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, Preact, and vanilla JavaScript.

The core pattern: a tool definition declares `_meta.ui.resourceUri`, which points to a `ui://` resource your server serves as HTML. Langdock fetches and renders it in a sandboxed iframe as a standalone output in the chat. On desktop, you can also open it in the side panel.

```typescript theme={null}
import {
  registerAppResource,
  registerAppTool,
  RESOURCE_MIME_TYPE,
} from "@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps/server";

const resourceUri = "ui://my-form";

registerAppTool(
  server,
  "render_form",
  {
    inputSchema: {},
    _meta: { ui: { resourceUri } },
  },
  async () => ({
    content: [{ type: "text", text: "Opening form..." }],
  }),
);

registerAppResource(
  server,
  resourceUri,
  resourceUri,
  { mimeType: RESOURCE_MIME_TYPE },
  async () => ({
    contents: [
      {
        uri: resourceUri,
        mimeType: RESOURCE_MIME_TYPE,
        text: "<html>...</html>",
      },
    ],
  }),
);
```

<CardGroup>
  <Card title="MCP Apps Documentation" icon="book" href="https://modelcontextprotocol.io/extensions/apps/overview">
    Official spec, SDK reference, and framework guides
  </Card>

  <Card title="ext-apps GitHub" icon="github" href="https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps">
    SDK source, examples, and issue tracker
  </Card>
</CardGroup>

## Example: ServiceNow MCP Server

The Langdock ServiceNow MCP Server is a reference implementation that shows how to combine OAuth Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) with MCP Apps forms for creating ServiceNow records from within Langdock.

It exposes four tools:

| Tool              | Description                                                                           |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `get_form_fields` | Retrieves available fields from a ServiceNow table                                    |
| `render_form`     | Returns an interactive MCP Apps form, optionally pre-filled from conversation context |
| `submit_form`     | Creates a record in ServiceNow from the submitted form data                           |
| `update_form`     | Updates fields in an existing ServiceNow form after `render_form` runs                |

<Card title="servicenow-mcp-server" icon="github" href="https://github.com/niklasmeixner-langdock/servicenow-mcp-server">
  Reference implementation — OAuth DCR + MCP Apps forms for ServiceNow
</Card>

## Connecting to Langdock

Once your MCP server is running, connect it to Langdock the same way as any MCP server. See the MCP integration guide for setup instructions, including authentication options.

# File Templates
Source: https://docs.langdock.com/en/using-langdock/library/file-templates

Upload documents and presentations as reusable templates. Share them when you want others to generate files in the same format and style.

<Frame>
  <img alt="The Create new file section in the Library with template cards and the All file templates button" />
</Frame>

File templates let you save existing documents or slide decks and reuse them as the starting point for new AI-generated files. When you start a new document or presentation in chat, you can pick a template. Langdock will generate the new file matching its format and style.

## Supported formats

Templates can be uploaded in the following formats:

| File type     | Extensions               |
| ------------- | ------------------------ |
| Presentations | `.pptx`, `.ppt`, `.potx` |
| Documents     | `.docx`, `.dotx`         |
| PDFs          | `.pdf`                   |

Maximum file size: **256 MB**

PDF templates you upload from your computer must be portrait. Landscape PDFs are rejected on that path. Upload the original `.pptx` or `.potx` instead.

## Browsing and using templates

### Opening the template gallery

From the [Library](/en/using-langdock/library/introduction), click **All file templates** under **Create new file** to open the template gallery. If you don't have a template yet, click **Add template**. You can also access templates directly when starting a new file in chat. Each mode (**Create document**, **Create presentation**) shows a **Use a template** section.

<Frame>
  <img alt="The File Templates gallery with ownership tabs, type filter, sort control, search field, Add template button, and a grid of template cards" />
</Frame>

### Filtering and sorting

The gallery lets you narrow down templates by:

* **Type**: All types, Presentation, or Document
* **Ownership**: All, Mine, or Shared with me
* **Sort**: Newest, A–Z, or most used

### Previewing a template

Click any template card to open a full-screen preview with a carousel of all pages. From the preview you can see the layout and content before committing to it.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Full-screen template preview showing the slides of a template and the Use this template button" />
</Frame>

### Using a template

Click **Use this template** in the preview to open a new chat with the template already attached. Langdock will use the template's format and style when generating your file.

<Frame>
  <img alt="A new chat in Create presentation mode with the Use a template section below the input and one template selected" />
</Frame>

### Attaching a template to an agent

You can attach file templates to an Agent so it can use them for matching document or presentation requests. In the Agent editor, open **Instructions**, then **More**, then **File templates**, and click **Add template**. After you attach one, **File templates** moves to its own row. Click the **X** on a template chip to remove it.

Alternatively, ask in the Agent Builder chat: *"Attach the quarterly report template to this agent"* or *"Remove the pitch deck template"*. The builder searches templates you have access to, attaches matching ones, and shows the change inline.

## Uploading a template

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open the template gallery">
    In the Library, click **All file templates** to open the gallery, then click the **+** button (Add template). You can also drag and drop a file directly onto the gallery dialog.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Upload your file">
    You have two ways to provide the file:

    * **From your computer**: select a file directly. Supported formats: `.pptx`, `.ppt`, `.potx`, `.docx`, `.dotx`, `.pdf` (max 256 MB).
    * **From a connected integration**: import from Google Drive, OneDrive, or another connected source using the integration picker in the upload dialog.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="The Upload template dialog with the Attach button, drag and drop hint, and supported formats" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Wait for analysis">
    Langdock analyzes the file and suggests instructions. The template name is taken from the filename. This takes a moment. You'll see a progress indicator while it runs.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="The upload dialog during analysis with a status message and progress bar" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Review and save">
    Check the name and instructions, edit them if needed, and click **Save**. The template is now available in the gallery for you and anyone you share it with.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="The upload review step showing the analysis banner, template name, and instructions fields" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Managing templates

Each template card has a context menu with the following actions:

<Frame>
  <img alt="A template card in the gallery with its context menu open, showing Edit, Share, Download, and Delete" />
</Frame>

| Action   | What it does                              |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Edit     | Change the template name and instructions |
| Share    | Share with specific users or groups       |
| Download | Download the original file                |
| Delete   | Remove the template permanently           |

**Edit**, **Share**, and **Delete** appear only when you have the required access.

## Sharing templates

You can share a template with individual users or groups in your workspace. New templates start as **Restricted**. Only people with access can use them until you share. Open the share dialog from the template card's context menu, search for users or groups, and confirm.

<Frame>
  <img alt="The template share dialog with people search, People with access list, and General access set to Restricted" />
</Frame>

Template sharing works like Skills sharing but uses its own permissions. There are two permissions in workspace roles that control what users can do:

* **Share templates**: Enabled for everyone by default. Any user can share a template with specific people or groups.
* **Share templates with workspace**: Admin-only by default. Only admins can make a template available to the entire workspace.

You can adjust these defaults in [User Management → Roles](https://app.langdock.com/settings/workspace/user-management/roles).

## Admin: enabling templates

Templates are built on top of Skills and require Skills to be enabled in your workspace. When Skills are disabled, templates will not appear in the Library or in chat.

By default, any user can share a template with specific users or groups, but only admins can share a template with the entire workspace. You can adjust both defaults under [User Management → Roles](https://app.langdock.com/settings/workspace/user-management/roles).

<Info>
  Go to **Settings → Products → Skills** to manage Skills availability for your workspace. On dedicated deployments, admins can additionally turn templates off with **Enable templates for this workspace** under **Settings → Workspace → Library**, even when Skills stay enabled.
</Info>

## FAQ

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Why can't I upload a template?">
    If you do not see the upload controls in the Library or in chat, your workspace role may not include the **Create skills** permission required to upload file templates. Ask a workspace admin to check this permission under [User management → Roles](https://app.langdock.com/settings/workspace/user-management/roles).
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Which template formats work best?">
    Templates work best when the structure is clear, reusable, and not overly dependent on fragile formatting. Use consistent headings, placeholders, and example content. Complex presentations or documents with strict brand layouts may require more testing and iteration.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="How should I prepare a reusable template?">
    Keep the template focused on the structure you want to preserve. Remove outdated content, use clear placeholder text, and include examples for sections that should be generated. If brand assets, fonts, or layout rules matter, include them directly in the template and describe the expected output in the prompt.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Why can generated documents or presentations differ from the template?">
    Generated files may differ when the model has to adapt content length, infer missing structure, or recreate formatting from ambiguous examples. More complex layouts, charts, tables, and presentations are more likely to need manual review or multiple iterations.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>


# Folders
Source: https://docs.langdock.com/en/using-langdock/library/folders

Create shared folders for files you want to work on with AI in chat.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Folders icon" />
</Frame>

Instead of attaching the same files to every chat, create a folder once, add the files you need, and open it from chat with **Work in a folder**. The model can read the files in the folder, help you compare or update them, and save generated files back when you have edit access.

Use Folders for active work: preparing a report with source material, reviewing a set of spreadsheets, collecting files for a project, or creating deliverables with your team. Use [Knowledge bases](/en/using-langdock/library/knowledge-bases) when you want semantic search across a larger document collection.

## Work in a folder from chat

Folders are most useful when the same set of files belongs to an ongoing task. Select a folder in chat, then ask the model to work with the files inside it.

For example, you can ask Langdock to:

* Prepare a weekly meeting from the agenda, project updates, feedback, and previous notes
* Summarize a spreadsheet and draft follow-up notes
* Create a presentation from files in the folder
* Update a document and save the result back to the folder

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open a chat">
    Start a new chat or open an existing one.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Sidebar menu with New chat selected" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Choose a folder">
    Click **Work in a folder** and select the folder you want to use.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Chat input with Work in a folder open and Weekly team meeting selected" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Work with the files in the folder">
    For example, ask the model to use the agenda, project updates, customer feedback, and previous notes to prepare the weekly team meeting. The model can summarize the files, list open questions, and draft follow-up tasks.
  </Step>
</Steps>

Any files in the selected folder are available to the chat. If you are an Editor or Owner of a folder, files generated in the chat can also be saved back to the folder.

Open image and supported document attachments directly from chat. See [Document Search](/en/using-langdock/chat/tools/document-search) for document previews and [Image Analysis](/en/using-langdock/chat/tools/image-analysis) for images.

## Create a folder and add files

You can create Folders from the [Library](/en/using-langdock/library/introduction). Open the Library from the left sidebar, find the Folders section, and click **Create folder**. To find an existing folder, use the search field next to **Create folder**. It filters the list by name as you type.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Folders section with the Create folder button selected" />
</Frame>

After you create a folder, add files from your computer, move files from [Recent Files](/en/using-langdock/library/recent-files), or move eligible attachments directly from chat. Folders are built for files you actively work with in Langdock, including documents, spreadsheets, presentations, images, and generated files. The model can visually analyze images in a folder, for example to describe a screenshot or read a diagram.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Upload from computer">
    1. Open your folder
    2. Click **Upload files** or drag files into the folder
    3. Wait until the files finish uploading
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Move from Recent Files">
    1. Open [Recent Files](/en/using-langdock/library/recent-files)
    2. Open the file menu
    3. Click **Move**
    4. Choose the destination folder
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Move from chat">
    1. Find the sent file card in chat. On desktop, hover over the card to show its actions
    2. Click **Move to folder** on the file card
    3. Choose a destination folder where you have Editor or Owner access
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

You can move only files you own that are not already in a Folder or Knowledge base. Files from synced integration folders cannot be moved this way.

<Note>
  Folders can contain up to **100 files** and **250 MB** total.
</Note>

## Share work with the right people

You can share folders with individuals, groups, or your entire workspace. Use Viewer access when someone should use files as context, and Editor access when they should also add, remove, or save files to your folder.

You need the **Share folders and knowledge bases with workspace** role permission to share a folder with your entire workspace.

| Permission                 | Owner | Editor | Viewer |
| -------------------------- | ----- | ------ | ------ |
| View folder and files      | ✓     | ✓      | ✓      |
| Use files in chat          | ✓     | ✓      | ✓      |
| Edit file contents         | ✓     | ✓      |        |
| Add files                  | ✓     | ✓      |        |
| Remove files               | ✓     | ✓      |        |
| Move files into the folder | ✓     | ✓      |        |
| Rename folder              | ✓     | ✓      |        |
| Share with others          | ✓     | ✓      |        |
| Delete folder              | ✓     |        |        |
| Transfer ownership         | ✓     |        |        |
| Leave folder               |       | ✓      | ✓      |

Owners must transfer ownership before they can leave a folder.

Workspace admins can only access Folders that are shared with them, with a group they belong to, or with the entire workspace. When a Folder is linked to a [Project](/en/using-langdock/chat/projects), the Project controls who can access the Folder. Such Folders cannot be shared separately.

## Choosing the right setup

Folders work best when you are actively working with a set of files. Use the options below when you want to collaborate on those files, give an Agent files to read or edit, or search across a larger document collection.

### Use a Project to collaborate on files

Use a [Project](/en/using-langdock/chat/projects) when several people should work with the same folder together. Everyone in the Project can use the project files as shared context in chat, and people with edit access can add files or save generated files back to the project folder.

You link a folder from the project itself with **Work in a folder**, either selecting an existing folder or creating a new one.

<Info>
  Removing a folder from a project does not delete the folder or its files. You can still find them in the Library.
</Info>

<Note>
  You can only attach a Folder to a Project when you are the Owner of both. After the Folder is linked, Project permissions control access to the folder.
</Note>

Use a Library Folder when the files should stay independent from a Project and be reused across different chats.

### Attach a Folder to an Agent

Attach a Library Folder when an Agent should keep using the same files. In the Agent editor, select **Add folders** in the **Folders** row, then choose the folder. Attached folders stay read-only until you mark one as a working folder.

To let the Agent edit and save files there, open the folder menu and select **Work in this folder**. The folder shows a **Working folder** badge. Publish the draft so new chats use it.

Working folders are available on workspace Agents, not Project Agents. Start the chat with the Agent. If you only add the Agent with @-mention, the working folder stays read-only.

You need edit access to the Agent and the folder to set this up. People chatting with the Agent need Editor or Owner access on the folder to save changes. When the Agent updates an existing file, it overwrites that file and stores a new version.

### Use a Knowledge base for search

Use a [Knowledge base](/en/using-langdock/library/knowledge-bases) when you need to find specific information across many documents. The model searches the Knowledge base for the most relevant sections and uses them as reference.

Use a Folder when you want to work with files directly. Use a Knowledge base when you want to search a larger collection for the right answer.

## FAQ

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="I cannot save generated files to a folder">
    Check that you have Editor or Owner access. Viewers can use folder files as context, but cannot save generated files there.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="I cannot edit a file in a folder">
    Files open as read-only documents when you have Viewer access. Ask the folder Owner or an Editor for edit access.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="I cannot add more files">
    Folders can contain up to 100 files and 250 MB total. Remove files or choose another folder before adding more.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="I cannot find my folder when choosing Work in a folder">
    Check that you have at least Viewer access to the folder. If the folder still does not appear, check the folder name and confirm that it still exists in the Library.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="I cannot upload a file">
    Check whether the file type is supported and whether the folder has reached the 100 files or 250 MB limit. Your workspace role also needs the **Upload documents** permission. If your uploads from the last 24 hours already exceed the default 2 GB cap, the next upload is blocked. Your deployment can use a higher configured cap. See [Supported file types](/en/using-langdock/troubleshooting/faq/supported-file-types) for the full list.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="I need to search across many documents">
    Use a [Knowledge base](/en/using-langdock/library/knowledge-bases) instead. Knowledge bases are built for semantic search across larger document collections.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="When should I use a folder?">
    Use folders to organize files you want to work with in Langdock, especially when several files belong to the same project or team workflow. Use Knowledge bases when the files should become a reusable searchable source for AI answers.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Are folders the same as Knowledge bases?">
    No. Folders help organize files in the Library. Knowledge bases are designed for retrieval, so Langdock can search relevant content and use it in chats, agents, workflows, or API usage.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>


# Introduction to Library
Source: https://docs.langdock.com/en/using-langdock/library/introduction

The Library is where you create files, manage Folders and Knowledge bases, and find generated and imported files in Recent Files.

<iframe title="Library overview video" />

The Library is your central hub for working with files in Langdock. It replaces scattered file access across individual chats and gives you one place to create, find, and organize everything. Whether you're starting a new document from scratch, reusing a team template, browsing files from past conversations, working in Folders, or managing Knowledge bases, it all lives here.

## What you find in the Library

### Create New File

Start a new document, spreadsheet, or presentation directly from the Library. Click **Blank file**, then choose **New document**, **New spreadsheet**, or **New presentation**. A new chat opens with the corresponding mode pre-selected.

<div>
  <img alt="The Create new file section showing the Blank file card with the file type menu open and templates next to it" />
</div>

If at least one template is available to you, you'll also see a row of templates here. Click **All file templates** to open the gallery, or **Add template** to upload one.

<Info>
  The Create new file section is only available when Skills and file templates are enabled in your workspace. See [File Templates](/en/using-langdock/library/file-templates) for details.
</Info>

### Folders

Folders are for active file work with AI in chat. Create a folder, add files, share access, then select it from chat with **Work in a folder**. The AI can use the folder files as context and save generated files back to the folder when you have edit access. Use the search field in the Folders section to filter folders and Knowledge bases by name as you type.

<Frame>
  <img alt="A Folder detail page with files and sharing controls" />
</Frame>

See [Folders](/en/using-langdock/library/folders) for details on creating, sharing, and using Folders in chat.

### Knowledge bases

Knowledge bases are searchable document collections for chat, Agents, Workflows, and the Knowledge Folder API. They appear in the Folders section alongside your regular folders. Use them for larger reference sets where the AI should find relevant sections through semantic search.

<Frame>
  <img alt="The Folders section in the Library, where Knowledge bases appear next to regular folders" />
</Frame>

See [Knowledge bases](/en/using-langdock/library/knowledge-bases) for details on creating, sharing, and searching Knowledge bases.

### Recent Files

Recent Files is your personal list of generated and imported files. Files stored in Folders, Knowledge bases, Projects, Agents, or synced integration folders do not appear here.

<img alt="The Recent Files section inside the Library" />

<Info>
  Recent Files follows your workspace's chat data retention settings. When a chat is deleted, only files associated with that chat are removed from Recent Files.
</Info>

See [Recent Files](/en/using-langdock/library/recent-files) for details on browsing, previewing, and managing your files.

## Getting to the Library

Click **Library** in the left sidebar to open it.

<div>
  <img alt="The Langdock sidebar with the Library item highlighted" />
</div>

## FAQ

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="When should I use the Library?">
    Use the Library to find and manage files, folders, templates, and Knowledge bases in Langdock. It is the place to organize reusable file-related assets instead of searching through individual chats.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="How is the Library different from a chat attachment?">
    A chat attachment is tied to the current conversation. Library items are easier to find, reuse, organize, and share depending on permissions and file type.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>


# Knowledge bases
Source: https://docs.langdock.com/en/using-langdock/library/knowledge-bases

Create searchable document collections for chat, Agents, Workflows, and the Knowledge Folder API.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Knowledge base icon" />
</Frame>

Knowledge bases help you find specific information across larger document collections. Instead of opening every file in chat, add your reference material once and use the Knowledge base when you need the model to search for the most relevant sections.

Use Knowledge bases for policies, handbooks, product documentation, support articles, manuals, and other reference material. Use [Folders](/en/using-langdock/library/folders) when you want to work directly with files, compare them, update them, or save generated files back.

<Info>
  Knowledge bases were previously called Knowledge Folders. The Knowledge Folder API keeps its existing endpoint names.
</Info>

## Search a Knowledge base from chat

Knowledge bases are most useful when you need an answer from a large set of reference documents. Select a Knowledge base in chat, then ask the model to find the information you need.

For example, you can ask Langdock to:

* Find the parental leave policy in an employee handbook
* Compare onboarding guidance across several internal documents
* Answer a support question from product documentation
* Find the right security policy for a customer questionnaire

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open a chat">
    Start a new chat or open an existing one.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Sidebar menu with New chat selected" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Choose a Knowledge base">
    Type `@`, search for the Knowledge base, and select it from the list.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Chat input with a Knowledge base selected" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Ask a question">
    For example, ask the model to find the parental leave policy in the employee handbook. The model searches the Knowledge base for relevant sections and answers from those sources.
  </Step>
</Steps>

When you use a Knowledge base in chat, Langdock searches for relevant sections from your documents. It does not send every document to the model.

## Create a Knowledge base and add documents

You can create Knowledge bases from the [Library](/en/using-langdock/library/introduction). Open the Library from the left sidebar, find the Folders section, click the arrow next to **Create folder**, and select **Create knowledge base**.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Folders section with the Create folder dropdown open and Create knowledge base selected" />
</Frame>

After you create a Knowledge base, upload documents from your computer or use the Knowledge Folder API for automated uploads. Knowledge bases are built for text-based reference material that should be searched later.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Upload from computer">
    1. Open your Knowledge base
    2. Click **Upload files** or drag documents into the Knowledge base
    3. Wait until the files finish processing
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="API upload">
    Use the Knowledge Folder API when you need to list Knowledge bases, manage access, rename them, or upload, update, delete, retrieve, or search files programmatically. For write operations, the API key itself needs the Editor role on the Knowledge base. The Viewer role covers search and retrieval.

    See the [Knowledge Folder API reference](/en/developer/knowledge-folder-api/sharing) for authentication, rate limits, and endpoint details.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Warning>
  Knowledge bases accept supported text-based formats such as PDF, DOCX, TXT, Markdown, and presentations. They do not accept tabular files, images, audio, or video.
</Warning>

<Note>
  Knowledge bases can contain up to **1,000 files**. Each file can contain up to **8 million characters**.
</Note>

## Share search access with the right people

You can share Knowledge bases with individuals, groups, or your entire workspace. Use Viewer access when someone should search documents, and Editor access when they should also add, remove, or manage documents.

You need the **Share folders and knowledge bases with workspace** role permission to share a Knowledge base with your entire workspace.

| Permission                        | Owner | Editor | Viewer |
| --------------------------------- | ----- | ------ | ------ |
| View Knowledge base and documents | ✓     | ✓      | ✓      |
| Search documents in chat          | ✓     | ✓      | ✓      |
| Use in Agents                     | ✓     | ✓      | ✓      |
| Add documents                     | ✓     | ✓      |        |
| Remove documents                  | ✓     | ✓      |        |
| Share with others                 | ✓     | ✓      |        |
| Delete Knowledge base             | ✓     | ✓      |        |

The person who creates a Knowledge base is its owner. Workspace admins have full control over all Knowledge bases, including changing the owner.

## Convert a Knowledge base to a folder

If you started with a Knowledge base but want to work with the files directly instead of searching them, you can convert it to a regular [folder](/en/using-langdock/library/folders). Files and sharing access move to the new folder, and the original Knowledge base is removed.

Convert a Knowledge base when you want to:

* Open files in chat, compare them, or edit them
* Save generated files back to the same location
* Add spreadsheets, images, or other file types that Knowledge bases don't accept

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open the Knowledge base">
    In the [Library](/en/using-langdock/library/introduction), open the Knowledge base you want to convert. You need Editor or Owner access.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Select Convert to folder">
    Open the more actions menu and select **Convert to folder**.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Confirm the conversion">
    Review the confirmation dialog, then confirm. The files and existing sharing access move to a new folder, and the Knowledge base is removed.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Note>
  Folders have lower limits than Knowledge bases: up to **100 files** and **250 MB** total. If your Knowledge base has more files, remove some before converting.
</Note>

<Warning>
  You can't convert a Knowledge base that's still connected through API access, Agents, chats, or Automations. Remove those connections first, then try again.
</Warning>

## Choosing the right setup

Knowledge bases work best when you need to search across many documents. Use the options below when you want to work directly with files or give an Agent access to the same reference material.

### Use a Folder to work with files

Use a [Folder](/en/using-langdock/library/folders) when you want to open files in chat, compare them, update them, or save generated files back. Folders are better for active work with a smaller set of files.

Use a Knowledge base when you want to search a larger collection for the right answer.

### Add a Knowledge base to an Agent for search

Add a Knowledge base to an [Agent](/en/using-langdock/agents/configuration) when the Agent should search the same reference material while answering. In the Agent editor, select **Add folders** in the **Folders** row, then choose the Knowledge base.

Use the **Files** row for files from your computer or individual files from integrations. Use the **Folders** row for Library Folders, Knowledge bases, and synced folders.

## FAQ

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="My Knowledge base is not appearing in @mentions">
    Check that you have at least Viewer access, then type more of the Knowledge base name to narrow the results.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="The model is not finding relevant information">
    Check that your documents finished processing, then rephrase your question with more specific terms. Verify that the information exists in the uploaded documents.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="I cannot upload certain file types">
    Knowledge bases accept supported text-based formats such as PDF, DOCX, TXT, Markdown, and presentations. Use a [Folder](/en/using-langdock/library/folders) when you need to work with spreadsheets, images, audio, or generated files.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="What should go into a Knowledge base instead of a direct attachment?">
    Use a Knowledge base for information that should be reused across chats, agents, workflows, or API usage. It is best for larger or longer-lived document collections where Langdock should search relevant sections instead of sending every file in full each time.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="How fresh is Knowledge base content?">
    Uploaded Knowledge base content is available after processing. If recent content is missing, check the processing status before assuming the model ignored the file. For automatically updated content, use [Folder Sync](/en/using-langdock/guides/integrations/folder-sync).
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Why are some files not searchable in a Knowledge base?">
    Files may not be searchable if the format is unsupported, the file failed processing, the content cannot be extracted reliably, or the source permissions prevent access. Spreadsheets and tabular data are not supported by Knowledge bases and should be used directly in chat instead.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>


# Recent Files
Source: https://docs.langdock.com/en/using-langdock/library/recent-files

Preview, download, and organize generated and imported files in your personal Recent Files list.

Recent Files is your personal list of generated and imported files in this workspace. Files other people created do not appear here.

<img alt="Recent Files in grid view showing file thumbnails with names and metadata" />

## What appears in Recent Files

Recent Files shows files based on their source:

| Source        | What it includes                                                                                             |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Generated** | Files created by Langdock in chat, including documents, presentations, spreadsheets, images, and code output |
| **Imported**  | Files pulled in from connected integrations                                                                  |

Files stored in Folders or Knowledge bases, files attached to Agents, Project files, files in synced integration folders, meeting recordings, workflow-only files, and files you upload in chat or in the Library are not shown here.

<Info>
  Recent Files follows your workspace's chat data retention settings. When a chat is deleted, only files associated with that chat are removed from Recent Files.
</Info>

## Grid and list view

Toggle between grid view (thumbnails) and list view (rows with details) using the view switcher in the top-right corner of the Recent Files section. Your preference is saved automatically.

## Filtering and sorting

Use the filter controls to narrow down files:

* **File type**: PDF, Document, Spreadsheet, Presentation, Image, or Code
* **Created**: Today, Yesterday, Last 7 days, or Last 30 days
* **Source**: Imported or Generated.

Use the search field to find files by name. Sort the list by Newest first, Oldest first, Name A-Z, or Name Z-A.

## File actions

Each file has a set of actions available from its context menu or action bar:

| Action               | Description                                   |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| Preview              | Open a preview of the file                    |
| Download             | Download the file                             |
| Start chat with file | Open a new chat with this file attached       |
| Move                 | Move the file into a Folder or Knowledge base |
| Delete file          | Remove the file permanently                   |

When a file comes from a chat, click the chat name on the file card or list row to open the original chat.

## File preview

Files can be previewed in these ways:

**Inline thumbnail.** Visible directly on each file card in grid view.

**Preview dialog.** Click a file to open a preview dialog without leaving the Library. Generated documents offer Word, PDF, and Markdown from the preview's download menu. When Google Drive, OneDrive, or SharePoint is connected, the preview toolbar can open the file with **Open in Google Drive**, **Open in OneDrive**, or **Open in SharePoint**.

**Full-screen.** Open the full-screen view for a larger preview. Multi-page files (documents, presentations) show a slide thumbnail strip for quick navigation. Presentations also support a presenter mode.

**Spreadsheet preview.** Open spreadsheets with sheet tabs, zoom, column resizing, and formula inspection.

## Batch actions

Select multiple files to enable batch actions in one of these ways:

* **Shift + click** to select a range of files
* In list view, hover over the list and click the checkbox in the header to select every file in the current view

Once files are selected, a bar appears at the bottom with options to:

* **Select all** to extend the selection to every visible file
* **Start chat with files**, up to 10 per chat
* **Download** all selected files
* **Move to folder**: moves all selected files into a Folder or Knowledge base at once
* **Delete** all selected files

<Tip>
  With **Select all**, you select every visible file that matches your active filters. Narrow the list by file type, date, or source before applying a batch action.
</Tip>

## Moving files to a Folder

Select **Move** from a file's context menu and choose the destination. You can also drag files onto a Folder or Knowledge base, or move files in bulk using batch selection.

Once you move a file into a Folder, open it in chat with **Work in a folder**. @mentions search Knowledge bases, not regular Folders. You can move a file into a Knowledge base when the file type is supported there.


# Excel Add-in
Source: https://docs.langdock.com/en/using-langdock/microsoft-add-ins/excel

With the Excel add-in you can work with Langdock without leaving your Excel workbook.

<iframe title="Excel Add-in overview" />

The Excel add-in brings Langdock into Microsoft Excel, so your spreadsheets and AI assistance stay side by side. Use it to understand workbooks faster, create formulas, clean up data, and turn spreadsheet findings into clear summaries without switching tools. You can ask questions while looking at your workbook, iterate on outputs directly in Excel, and keep your analysis in the place where the work is happening.

## How to install Langdock for Excel

Install the Langdock Add-in from the Microsoft Marketplace and connect it to your Langdock account.

<Note>
  Before you can use the Excel add-in, an admin needs to enable it in the workspace integration settings. If it is not enabled yet, point your admin to the [Add-in Setup Guide](/en/admin/manage-integrations/add-in-setup-guides/excel).
</Note>

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open the Microsoft Marketplace">
    Navigate to the [Langdock for Excel](https://marketplace.microsoft.com/en-us/product/office/WA200011245?tab=Overview) page on the Microsoft Marketplace.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Langdock for Excel listing on the Microsoft Marketplace with the Get it now button" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Get the Add-in">
    Click **Get it now** and confirm your details in the dialog that appears.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Confirm your details dialog for Langdock for Excel with the Get it now button" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Open in Excel">
    Click **Open in Excel** to launch the Add-in directly in your workbook.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Langdock for Excel launch page with the Open in Excel button" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Sign in to Langdock">
    Follow the sign-in flow to connect the Add-in to your Langdock account. Click **Continue** to log in.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Langdock sign-in screen for Microsoft Excel with the Continue button" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>
</Steps>

You can now use Langdock while your workbook stays open. Start with a specific question about what you want to understand, calculate, clean up, or explain.

## Working with Langdock in Excel

The Excel add-in is useful whenever the work starts in a spreadsheet. Instead of copying data into a separate chat, you can keep Excel open and use Langdock alongside it.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Excel add-in card showing the Excel icon and text Use Langdock inside of Microsoft Excel" />
</Frame>

### Common use cases

* **Build tables and plans**: Ask Langdock to create budget plans, project trackers, comparison tables, reporting templates, or charts directly in your workbook.
* **Create calculations**: Describe the calculation you need and let Langdock add formulas, totals, percentages, or growth rates.
* **Clean and structure data**: Standardize names, dates, categories, currencies, or messy rows before you analyze them.
* **Analyze spreadsheet results**: Ask Langdock to find trends, outliers, changes, and key takeaways in your data.
* **Research and enrichment**: Use Langdock to research companies, markets, or topics and add useful context to your spreadsheet.
* **Prepare summaries**: Turn spreadsheet findings into updates for reports, emails, presentations, or team meetings.

### Example: Build a quarterly budget plan

Say you need to create a quarterly budget plan with department-level cost breakdowns. Open the Langdock Add-in next to your workbook and describe what you want to build.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Excel workbook with the Langdock Add-in open next to an empty spreadsheet" />
</Frame>

Ask Langdock for the spreadsheet you need:

`Build a quarterly budget plan with department-level cost breakdowns`

<Frame>
  <img alt="Langdock Add-in in Excel with a prompt asking for a quarterly budget plan with department-level cost breakdowns" />
</Frame>

Langdock creates the table in your workbook and keeps the conversation open next to it. From there, you can ask follow-up questions, analyze the table, perform calculations, or use connected integrations without leaving Excel.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Excel workbook with a quarterly budget table and Langdock summarizing the results in the Add-in panel" />
</Frame>

### Jump to cited cells

When Langdock references cells in a reply, the reference appears as a clickable pill, for example **Sheet1 B3:B8**. Click the pill to open the referenced sheet and select the range in your workbook. If the sheet has since been renamed or removed, Langdock shows a short notice instead.

### Import an uploaded spreadsheet

Attach a spreadsheet to the chat and ask Langdock to open, import, insert, or edit it in Excel, for example `Import this spreadsheet into my workbook`. Langdock copies the attached workbook's sheets into the workbook you have open so you can review and edit them in place. Without an explicit request, the attachment stays a read-only data source and your workbook stays unchanged. Importing never modifies the uploaded file or its source in OneDrive, SharePoint, or Google Drive.

### Next steps

After Langdock creates the first output, you can keep working from the same panel:

* Ask follow-up questions about the sheet
* Add calculations, totals, or comparisons
* Enrich the spreadsheet with results from a [Web Search](/en/using-langdock/chat/tools/web-search)
* Draft an email by using [Actions in Chat](/en/using-langdock/chat/tools/actions-in-chat) and selecting your email provider from your connected [integrations](/en/using-langdock/integrations/introduction)

## Edit permissions

Langdock asks before changing your workbook by default. Switch modes from the **Edit permissions** menu in the chat input:

* **Ask before edits**: Langdock shows a confirmation with the action and, when available, the target range before each write. Choose **Allow once**, **Always allow** for the current chat, or **Deny**.
* **Accept all edits**: Langdock applies edits without asking.

When Langdock writes cells or copies a range, it does not overwrite cells that already have data unless you explicitly ask to replace or change them. Other workbook operations follow your request and the confirmation mode you selected. Formulas that fetch external data or open links are always rejected.

## Save to Library

You can save the open workbook directly to your Langdock Library. Choose a [Folder](/en/using-langdock/library/folders) you can edit. Other people can access the saved workbook when that Folder is shared with them. Saving to the Library root does not add the file to [Recent Files](/en/using-langdock/library/recent-files).

<Frame>
  <img alt="Save to Library dropdown in the Excel add-in" />
</Frame>

## Preferences

Open the add-in menu in the top bar and select **Preferences** to customize the add-in. Two settings shape how your add-in chats behave:

* **Instructions**: Add custom instructions that apply only to chats in the Excel add-in, for example `Round decimals to two places`.
* **Default model**: New add-in chats start on [**Auto mode**](/en/using-langdock/models-and-limits/models#auto-mode). After you pick another model, **Reset** takes you back to **Auto mode**.

Both are independent of your global [account settings](/en/using-langdock/account/account). You can also switch the theme and delete all add-in conversations here.


# Outlook Add-in
Source: https://docs.langdock.com/en/using-langdock/microsoft-add-ins/outlook

With the Outlook add-in you can work with Langdock without leaving your Outlook inbox or calendar.

The Outlook add-in brings Langdock into Microsoft Outlook, so your email, calendar, and AI assistance stay side by side. Use it to catch up on a full inbox, get the key points from long threads, draft replies, and prepare your meetings without switching tools. Langdock knows which email or calendar event you have open, so you can ask about it directly instead of copying content into a separate chat.

## How to install Langdock for Outlook

Install the Langdock Add-in from the Microsoft Marketplace and connect it to your Langdock account. The add-in is available in Outlook on the web and desktop.

<Note>
  Before you can use the Outlook add-in, an admin needs to enable it in the workspace integration settings. If it is not enabled yet, point your admin to the [Add-in Setup Guide](/en/admin/manage-integrations/add-in-setup-guides/outlook).
</Note>

<Steps>
  <Step title="Get the Add-in">
    Navigate to the [Langdock for Outlook](https://marketplace.microsoft.com/en-us/product/WA200011534?tab=Overview) page on the Microsoft Marketplace, click **Get it now**, and confirm your details in the dialog that appears.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Langdock for Outlook listing on the Microsoft Marketplace with the Get it now button" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Open in Outlook">
    After the Add-in is added to your account, click **Open in Outlook Web**.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Langdock for Outlook confirmation page with the Open in Outlook Web button" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Sign in to Langdock">
    Return to your inbox, open an email, and click **Langdock** in the Outlook toolbar. Without an open email, the apps in the toolbar are disabled. Click **Continue** and sign in through your browser. Copy the sign-in code, paste it into the **Complete sign-in** screen in Outlook, then click **Continue**.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Langdock sign-in screen for Microsoft Outlook with the Continue button" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Connect Outlook">
    On the **Connect Outlook** screen, click **Connect** for Outlook Email and Outlook Calendar. The add-in uses these two integrations to read message content, search your mailbox, and work with your calendar. If both integrations are already connected in Langdock, this screen is skipped.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Pin the pane">
    Click the pin icon at the top of the Langdock pane. Outlook closes an unpinned pane when you switch between emails. A new compose window also opens without the pane, so pin it there once as well.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Apps pane in Outlook with Langdock listed and the pin icon at the top" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>
</Steps>

You can now use Langdock while Outlook stays open. Start with a specific question about the email or calendar event you are viewing.

<Warning>
  Connect Outlook Email and Outlook Calendar with the same Microsoft account you use in Outlook. Otherwise Langdock works with a different inbox and calendar than the one in front of you. Skipping the connection is fine, you can always catch up on it later. Until then, Langdock can use details from the open item such as the subject, participants, timing, location, and attachment names, plus what you have typed into an open draft. It cannot search your mailbox or calendar or read the body of a received message until the matching integration is connected.
</Warning>

## Working with Langdock in Outlook

The Outlook add-in is useful whenever the work starts in your inbox or calendar. Open an email or a calendar event, open Langdock next to it, and ask for what you need.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Outlook add-in card showing the Outlook icon and text Use Langdock inside of Microsoft Outlook" />
</Frame>

### Common use cases

* **Catch up on your inbox**: Get a summary of what came in and what needs your attention.
* **Summarize long threads**: Pull the key points, open questions, and next steps out of a conversation without rereading every message.
* **Draft replies**: Ask for a response based on the open thread, then refine tone and content in the chat.
* **Compose new emails**: Ask Langdock to write or expand a draft. It can fill in the body, the subject, and the recipients.
* **Organize your inbox**: Sort messages into folders and clear out what's done.
* **Plan your week**: Check your schedule, and create or update calendar events from the same conversation.

### Example: Research stats and draft the reply

Say a colleague asks for something you would normally research in a separate chat. Sarah is building a deck for a customer webinar and needs three current stats on how teams use AI at work, each with a source she can cite. Open the email, click **Reply** to open a draft, then open Langdock next to the draft and describe what you need.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Email with a research request open in Outlook and the Langdock pane with the prompt typed in the chat input" />
</Frame>

Ask Langdock for the research and the reply in one prompt:

`Find credible stats on how teams use AI at work and draft my reply with the numbers and their sources and then draft the reply to Sarah`

<Frame>
  <img alt="Langdock pane in Outlook running a web search for the requested statistics" />
</Frame>

Langdock searches the web, collects the numbers with their sources, and writes the reply into the draft. You review the text in Outlook exactly as it will be sent, with every stat linked to its source.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Reply draft in Outlook written by Langdock with three sourced statistics and the Langdock pane explaining the numbers" />
</Frame>

In the chat, Langdock summarizes which numbers it used and flags the caveats. From there, keep refining: make it shorter, adjust the tone, or add a second source.

### Next steps

After the first response, you can keep working from the same panel:

* Ask follow-up questions about the thread or event
* Use your [Skills](/en/using-langdock/guides/skills/skills-guide) to draft replies that follow your team's writing guidelines
* Enrich your reply with results from a [Web Search](/en/using-langdock/chat/tools/web-search)
* Work with your connected [integrations](/en/using-langdock/integrations/introduction) without leaving Outlook

## Edit permissions

Langdock always asks before changing an open draft by default. You can switch from **Ask before edits** to **Accept all edits** in the **Edit permissions** menu in the chat input.

When Langdock wants to write into the draft, the **Edit Outlook draft?** dialog shows the fields it is about to change:

* **Allow once**: Applies the edit. Langdock asks again for the next one.
* **Always allow edits**: Applies the edit and skips the dialog for the rest of the current chat.
* **Deny**: Rejects the edit and leaves the draft unchanged.

In both modes, edits apply only to the open draft and never send it. Langdock sends an email or invitation only when you ask it to and confirm the action.

## Preferences

Open the add-in menu in the top bar and select **Preferences** to customize the add-in. Two settings shape how your add-in chats behave:

* **Instructions**: Add custom instructions that apply only to chats in the Outlook add-in, for example `Keep replies short and to the point`.
* **Default model**: New add-in chats start on [**Auto mode**](/en/using-langdock/models-and-limits/models#auto-mode). After you pick another model, **Reset** takes you back to **Auto mode**.

Both are independent of your global [account settings](/en/using-langdock/account/account). You can also switch the theme and delete all add-in conversations here.


# Context Window
Source: https://docs.langdock.com/en/using-langdock/models-and-limits/context-window

Learn how chat context works, how the context window indicator helps you manage it, and how context usage differs from usage limits.

The context window is the information the model can use for its next response. In Langdock, it includes the current chat, the context you add, and the tools Langdock prepares for the model.

You can use the context window indicator to see how much space remains in the selected model's context window. It helps you understand what is taking up space and when it is worth reducing context or starting fresh.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Chat input with the context window indicator open above the model selector" />
</Frame>

## What fills the context window

Langdock builds the context window from the information the model needs to answer. Depending on the chat, it can include:

* Your messages and the model's responses
* Files, images, and other attachments in the chat, including files from [Folders](/en/using-langdock/library/folders)
* Relevant sections from [Knowledge bases](/en/using-langdock/library/knowledge-bases)
* Relevant [Memory](/en/using-langdock/chat/tools/memory)
* Active [Skills](/en/using-langdock/skills/introduction)
* System instructions and tool instructions
* Tool calls and tool results from [Web Search](/en/using-langdock/chat/tools/web-search), file reading, [integrations](/en/using-langdock/chat/tools/actions-in-chat), and other tools
* Summaries of earlier chat history when a long conversation is summarized

This is why a short follow-up can still use a lot of context. The model receives your latest message together with the surrounding chat state it needs to answer.

## Context window indicator

Check the indicator before long follow-ups or uploading large attachments. If the current chat already uses a lot of context, start a fresh chat with a short recap so the model has more room for your next task.

### 1. Open the indicator

Find the circular indicator next to the model selector in the chat input. Click it to open the context window panel.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Chat input with the context window indicator selected next to the model selector" />
</Frame>

### 2. Check current context and usage

The top row gives you a quick check of the current chat. It shows used context, total context window size, and the percentage used for the selected model.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Collapsed context window indicator showing context used, free space, session limit, and weekly usage" />
</Frame>

#### Usage limit indicator

The `Usage` section gives you a quick overview of your current usage limits:

* `Session limit` shows your usage in the current 5-hour window and when it resets.
* `Weekly usage` shows your usage in the current weekly window and when it resets.
* `Extra usage` appears when extra usage applies to your Workspace.

These rows are separate from context window usage. Context window usage shows how much room remains in the current chat. Usage limits show how much of your plan allowance you have used over time. For the full explanation of usage windows, fallback behavior, and increasing your limits, see [Usage Limits](/en/using-langdock/models-and-limits/fair-usage-policy).

### 3. Understand your context window

You can expand the `Context window` row to see a breakdown of how the context window is used and understand which categories take up the most space. Hover over `Other tools` to see which tools are grouped there.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Expanded context window indicator showing system tools, system prompt, messages, tool rows, memory, summarized conversation, attachments, and free space" />
</Frame>

<Note>
  Token values are estimates. Use them to understand relative context usage. They may differ from provider billing or exact model tokenization.
</Note>

The context indicator shows the categories that are relevant to your current chat. The table below explains what each category means when it appears in the breakdown.

| Category                  | What it means                                                                                            |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `System tools`            | Tool definitions Langdock includes so the model knows which tools it can use.                            |
| `System prompt`           | Instructions and system context that guide how the model should respond.                                 |
| `Messages`                | The parts of your conversation history that are still included for the next response.                    |
| `Skills`                  | Instructions from active [Skills](/en/using-langdock/skills/introduction) that are loaded into the chat. |
| `Relevant Memory`         | [Memory](/en/using-langdock/chat/tools/memory) entries Langdock includes for the current chat.           |
| `Summarized conversation` | A shorter summary of older chat history included after Langdock optimises a long conversation.           |
| `Attachments / images`    | Images and attachment content included in the current context.                                           |
| `Tool rows`               | Named tool calls and results, such as `Web search`, `Read file`, or `Email`.                             |
| `Other tools`             | Additional tool calls grouped under one row.                                                             |
| `Tool results`            | Tool output that counts toward context but is not shown under a specific named tool row.                 |
| `Free space`              | Estimated room left in the selected model's context window.                                              |

## Conversation optimisation

Langdock can optimise long chats so you can keep working without starting over.

Your full chat history stays visible, so you can always scroll back and read earlier messages. During conversation optimisation, Langdock summarizes older parts of the conversation for the model so the chat can continue within the context window. If an exact detail still matters, mention it again before you continue.

| What you see                                             | What it means                                                            |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Optimizing our conversation so we can continue working` | Langdock is preparing a shorter version of older context for the model.  |
| `Conversation optimised`                                 | Optimisation is complete, and the chat can continue.                     |
| `Summarized conversation`                                | The context window indicator includes the summary of older chat history. |

<Note>
  Optimisation is based on context size, not message count. A short chat with large files, tool results, or retrieved knowledge can fill the context window faster than a long plain-text chat.
</Note>

## Managing your context window

Use the indicator to decide when to reduce context, summarize the important details, or start a fresh chat.

* Start a new chat when you move to a new topic.
* Remove unnecessary files or images before sending the next message.
* Reference specific sections instead of attaching entire documents when possible.
* Use consistent terms so the model can connect related parts of the conversation.
* Refer to important details directly, such as "use the pricing section we discussed earlier".
* Add a short recap before continuing a long chat.
* Choose a model with a larger context window when the task requires long documents or extended analysis.

<Tip>
  If a chat starts producing less focused answers, start a new chat with a short summary of the important context. This gives the model more room for the next task.
</Tip>

## FAQ

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Does conversation optimisation delete my messages?">
    No. Your messages stay visible in the chat. The model may receive a summary of older messages instead of the full earlier conversation.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Why did the model forget something we discussed earlier?">
    The chat may have exceeded what fits in the model's context window. Older details can become less reliable after a long conversation is summarized, especially in chats with files, tools, Agents, or large amounts of retrieved knowledge.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Why can this happen after only a few messages?">
    Context is based on tokens, not message count. A few large prompts, attached files, retrieved knowledge, system instructions, or tool results can fill the context window quickly. Break larger tasks into smaller chats or phases, and bring only the files and instructions needed for the next step.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="When should I use files or Knowledge bases instead of chat history?">
    Use files when information needs to stay durable or quoted exactly later. Use [Knowledge bases](/en/using-langdock/library/knowledge-bases) when information needs to stay searchable across many documents. Chat history is useful for conversation flow, but it is not a reliable long-term knowledge store after older context is summarized.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="What does conversation optimization mean?">
    Conversation optimization means older parts of a long conversation may be compacted so the chat can continue within the model's context window. The visible chat history is not deleted, but the model may no longer receive every older message word for word.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Why did the assistant forget something from earlier in the chat?">
    The conversation may have exceeded what the model can consider at once. Older details can become summarized, omitted, or less reliable, especially in long chats or chats with large files, retrieved knowledge, tools, or agent actions.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="How is the context window different from output and usage limits?">
    The context window controls how much information the model can read for one request. Output limits control how much the model can write in one response. Usage limits control how much model capacity a user or workspace can consume.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>


# Usage Limits
Source: https://docs.langdock.com/en/using-langdock/models-and-limits/fair-usage-policy

Understand how usage is measured, what your limits are, and what happens when you reach them.

When you use chat and agents, your usage is measured based on the tokens your prompts and responses consume and the token prices of the model. Models that use more tokens or have higher token prices consume your limit faster than lightweight ones. The model selector shows a **Usage consumption** rating for each model, with an explanation of how it is calculated. Today's models are fundamentally more powerful than what existed even a year ago. They can write full documents, build presentations, run multi-step research, and handle complex tasks end to end. So what are the limits, and how do you make the most of them?

This page explains how usage limits work and what happens when you reach them. For tips on getting the most out of your Langdock subscription, see [Usage Tips](/en/using-langdock/models-and-limits/usage-tips).

## Usage windows

Your usage is tracked across two time windows:

| Window      | Duration         | How it works                                                   |
| ----------- | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Session** | 5 hours          | Starts when you send your first message. Resets after 5 hours. |
| **Weekly**  | Monday to Monday | Fixed weekly window. Resets every Monday.                      |

Both windows have their own limit. If Extra Usage is enabled and available, you can continue using your selected model after reaching an included limit. Without available Extra Usage, your messages use a fallback model until that window resets. In Langdock Cloud workspaces without BYOK, the fallback is GPT-5.6 Luna. In BYOK and Dedicated Deployments, the fallback is the model configured for your workspace. A workspace spend limit can trigger this fallback before included usage is exhausted.

These limits also apply to tools such as Document Editor, Company Knowledge, and Deep Research, as well as to messages in builder chats such as the Workflow Builder.

## Checking your usage

You can check your usage directly from chat to see how much of your current session and weekly limits you have used. This helps you manage your usage and decide when to switch models, continue later, or adjust your plan.

### 1. Open the indicator

Find the circular indicator next to the model selector in the chat input. Click it to open the context window panel.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Chat input with the context window indicator selected next to the model selector" />
</Frame>

### 2. Check your usage limits

The `Usage` section shows your current usage limits:

* `Session limit` shows your usage in the current 5-hour window and when it resets.
* `Weekly usage` shows your usage in the current weekly window and when it resets.
* `Extra usage` appears when extra usage applies to your Workspace.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Context window indicator showing session limit and weekly usage progress" />
</Frame>

### Check usage in account settings

You can also see your current usage in [Settings > Account > Usage](https://app.langdock.com/settings/account/usage). On Langdock Cloud, the page is available to all members. In BYOK and Dedicated Deployments, it is available when your account has a finite included usage limit. The page shows progress bars for both your session and weekly usage, along with the time until each window resets.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Account usage settings showing current session and weekly usage progress bars with percentages and reset times" />
</Frame>

## Tips to get the most out of your usage

We've put together a [Usage Tips](/en/using-langdock/models-and-limits/usage-tips) guide to help you and your team get the most out of Langdock, with practical tips on model selection, prompting, and how to work efficiently within your limits.

## What happens when you reach a limit

When you hit your session or weekly limit, available Extra Usage lets you continue using your selected model. Without available Extra Usage, your messages use a fallback model until that window resets. In Langdock Cloud workspaces without BYOK, the fallback is GPT-5.6 Luna. In BYOK and Dedicated Deployments, the fallback is the model configured for your workspace. A workspace spend limit can trigger this fallback before included usage is exhausted.

If your admin has enabled usage requests, you will see a **Request higher limits** button in the chat. Your admin will be notified and can increase your limits or upgrade your plan.

<Info>
  If you reach a limit while the model is working, it is allowed to finish its response before switching. You won't see a reply cut off halfway. Your next message uses your available Extra Usage or the configured fallback behavior.
</Info>

## Increasing your limits

Your usage limits depend on the plan you are on. If you regularly hit your limits, your admin can:

* [Upgrade you to a higher plan](/en/admin/manage-usage/plans) with more usage.
* [Enable pay-as-you-go billing](/en/admin/manage-usage/extra-usage) so you can keep using premium models after reaching your limit.

***

There is also a spam protection limit of 250 messages per 3 hours, regardless of model cost. This limit exists to prevent automated abuse and does not affect normal usage.

*Last updated: April 2026*

## FAQ

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="How is usage measured?">
    Usage is based on the resources consumed by model requests, not just the number of messages. Long chats, large files, stronger models, tool use, and generated output can all increase usage because the model processes more input, produces more output, or uses more expensive capabilities.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="What happens when I reach my usage limit?">
    When a usage limit is reached, available Extra Usage lets you continue using your selected model. Without available Extra Usage, your messages use a fallback model until the usage window resets. In Langdock Cloud workspaces without BYOK, the fallback is GPT-5.6 Luna. In BYOK and Dedicated Deployments, the fallback is the model configured for your workspace. A workspace spend limit can trigger this fallback before included usage is exhausted.
